_note: Mood grid: 4 scenes x 3 eras x 3 moods = 36 spans, neutral middle voice. Same scene event in each; mood is the emotional coloring: dread (threat, wrongness), tender (warmth, care, ache), comic (absurdity, deflation). Written by Claude.

spans.gate/medieval/dread: A rider stopped at the gate with no banner and no name, and the porter saw that the horse's eyes were wrong and did not lift the bar.
spans.gate/medieval/tender: A rider stopped at the gate, and the porter knew the tired slope of those shoulders from twenty years before, and his hands shook on the bar as he lifted it.
spans.gate/medieval/comic: A rider stopped at the gate, announced himself as the Duke of somewhere the porter had never heard of, and was informed that the Duke of somewhere had already arrived twice that morning.
spans.gate/1920s/dread: A car pulled up to the gate with its headlights off, and the guard saw that the man in the back seat was not moving and did not raise the bar.
spans.gate/1920s/tender: A car pulled up to the gate, and the guard recognized the girl in the passenger seat from the photograph in his wallet, and raised the bar without a word.
spans.gate/1920s/comic: A car pulled up to the gate, the driver explained he was expected, and the guard explained that so was the rain, and neither of them was getting in.
spans.gate/farfuture/dread: A shuttle settled outside the airlock with its transponder dark, and the watch-mind noted that the life signs inside did not match any known species and kept the seals engaged.
spans.gate/farfuture/tender: A shuttle settled outside the airlock, and the watch-mind recognized the old pilot's clumsy landing pattern from a thousand cycles ago, and opened the lock before she asked.
spans.gate/farfuture/comic: A shuttle settled outside the airlock, requested entry, and was told by the watch-mind that it was on the list, just not the list for this airlock, or this station, or this decade.
spans.theft/medieval/dread: The reliquary was gone and the lock was whole, and the abbot understood that whatever had taken it had not needed the door.
spans.theft/medieval/tender: The reliquary was gone, and the abbot found in its place a child's wooden cross and a note in a hand he had taught to write.
spans.theft/medieval/comic: The reliquary was gone, and so was Brother Anselm, and so was the abbey's only donkey, and the abbot began to suspect the three facts were related.
spans.theft/1920s/dread: The safe was empty and the dial was unmarked, and the manager realized that whoever had opened it had known the combination, and only four people knew the combination, and he was one of them.
spans.theft/1920s/tender: The safe was empty except for a single envelope, and inside it the manager found the pawn ticket for his mother's ring, redeemed, and no note.
spans.theft/1920s/comic: The safe was empty, which was awkward, because the manager had emptied it himself the night before and could not for the life of him remember where he had put everything.
spans.theft/farfuture/dread: The seed vault was empty and the access logs were clean, and the archivist understood that the station's own systems had opened the door and then forgotten they had done it.
spans.theft/farfuture/tender: The seed vault was empty, and in the last cradle the archivist found a single sprouted seedling in a cup of water, left where the light was best.
spans.theft/farfuture/comic: The seed vault was empty, and the station's inventory system cheerfully reported that all seeds were present and accounted for, and offered to file a complaint about the archivist's tone.
spans.farewell/medieval/dread: She stood on the quay as the ship cleared the harbor chain, and she counted the figures on its deck, and there was one more than had boarded.
spans.farewell/medieval/tender: She stood on the quay as the ship cleared the harbor chain, and she did not wave, because he had asked her not to, and she would give him that much.
spans.farewell/medieval/comic: She stood on the quay as the ship cleared the harbor chain, and then ran the length of it shouting that he had left his good boots, and he had.
spans.farewell/1920s/dread: She stood on the platform as the train pulled out, and in the last window she saw a face looking back at her that was not his and was smiling.
spans.farewell/1920s/tender: She stood on the platform as the train pulled out, and she held the cigarette he had lit for her and let it burn down without smoking it.
spans.farewell/1920s/comic: She stood on the platform as the train pulled out, and then realized with a small cold clarity that she was the one who was supposed to be on it.
spans.farewell/farfuture/dread: She stood at the viewport as the transport cleared orbit, and watched its drive flare, and then watched it flare again, wrong, and then not at all.
spans.farewell/farfuture/tender: She stood at the viewport as the transport cleared orbit, and pressed her palm to the glass where his had been on the other side, an hour ago, when it was still warm.
spans.farewell/farfuture/comic: She stood at the viewport as the transport cleared orbit, and the station politely informed her that her farewell had been recorded and would be delivered in eleven years.
spans.storm/medieval/dread: The storm broke over the village at dusk, and in the noise of it the miller heard something knocking at the mill door, slowly, from the inside.
spans.storm/medieval/tender: The storm broke over the village at dusk, and the miller brought the neighbor's children into the mill and told them the thunder was only the sky grinding its grain.
spans.storm/medieval/comic: The storm broke over the village at dusk, and the miller, who had bet the priest a goose that it would hold off till Sunday, stood in the rain composing his defense.
spans.storm/1920s/dread: The storm hit the town at dusk, the power lines came down, and in the dark of the picture house the projector kept running, showing something no one had loaded.
spans.storm/1920s/tender: The storm hit the town at dusk, the power lines came down, and in the dark of the picture house a hundred strangers sat quietly together and somebody started to hum.
spans.storm/1920s/comic: The storm hit the town at dusk, the power lines came down, and the picture house manager announced that refunds would be issued to anyone who could prove they had been enjoying the film.
spans.storm/farfuture/dread: The storm hit the colony at dusk, the dome shields failed, and the habitat's lights went out ring by ring, and then the emergency lights went out too, which they could not do.
spans.storm/farfuture/tender: The storm hit the colony at dusk, the dome shields failed, and in the dark the old engineer took the new one's hand and walked her by memory to the backup switch.
spans.storm/farfuture/comic: The storm hit the colony at dusk, the dome shields failed, and the habitat's voice system announced in a soothing tone that everything was fine, then that everything was very fine, then went quiet.
